q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Short answer — the system could not identify a single causal trigger. Net sales on 2026-10-12 were unusually low versus your typical days (−59.8% vs “usual”), but they were actually higher than 2026-10-11. The drop (vs usual) is concentrated in Meta / ig_feed and a few campaigns that went to zero; candidate correlates (sessions, ad spend, add‑to‑carts) moved with the day but were not proven causes.

Key evidence (previous day → 2026-10-12)
- Net sales: 2026-10-11 ₹34,377 → 2026-10-12 ₹42,177. Measured  
- Usual (reference level): usual ₹104,860 → 2026-10-12 ₹42,177 (−59.8% vs usual). Measured/Derived  
- Gross sales: ₹36,166 → ₹46,782. Measured  
- Ad spend (P&L basis): ₹40,080 → ₹38,661. Measured  
- Sessions: 3,423 → 3,254. Measured  
- Impressions: 153,941 → 133,021. Measured  
- Add‑to‑cart events: 282 → 317. Measured

What the diagnosis found
- Where it sat: the shortfall versus “usual” is concentrated in channel sub_channel=ig_feed (≈71% of the deviation). Measured  
- Specific places outside normal: campaign TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ (and ad TH-383-SUSPENDER-4XL‑MAROON_…) went from ~₹6,488 to ₹0. Measured  
- Tested drivers: sessions, ad_spend and add‑to‑carts are implicated (same‑day correlation), but the causal tests did NOT meet the bar to call any of them the cause. Measured / Hypothesis

Bottom line — we know what changed and where (ig_feed / the listed campaigns), but the automated causal analysis could not prove why (no upstream cause met the threshold). Next useful step: drill into ig_feed and the specific campaigns/adsets (delivery, budget, disapproved ads or paused campaigns) — shall I run a channel + campaign drilldown for 2026-10-12?
